title: Rahul Builders v. Sunrise Hotels
text: The plaintiff, Rahul Builders, seeks specific performance of an agreement for sale of immovable property entered into with the defendant, Sunrise Hotels, for a consideration of Rs 8 crore. The defendant refused to execute the sale deed on the agreed date claiming the consideration was inadequate at current market rates. The defendant's refusal constitutes breach of contract. The plaintiff duly tendered the full consideration amount on the stipulated date. Under Section 10 of the Specific Relief Act, specific performance of a contract to transfer immovable property may be ordered where damages are not an adequate remedy. Real property has unique value and damages would not adequately compensate the plaintiff. The court grants a decree of specific performance directing the defendant to execute the sale deed within 60 days. The plaintiff shall deposit the balance consideration amount in court. Breach of contract in this case entitles the plaintiff to specific performance as the primary relief.
